rounds.text: Sunil Healthcare Ltd trades at a highly attractive price-to-book ratio of just 1.10x on a book value of ₹ 66.1 against a share price of ₹ 72.4 [E2], and this is further underscored by a provider-reported P/B of 1.37x which sits at a steep discount to the sector benchmark of 2.73x [E7]. Fundamental performance has notably outpaced stock action, with profit growing at 65% compared to a mere 14% price growth over a 5-year period [E52], showing that the underlying earnings power is significantly under-appreciated by the current market capitalisation of ₹ 74.3 Cr [E3]. This earnings-led value disconnect is widening further as recent profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by an astounding 1253%, signalling that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E53]. Reinforcing this positive shift, capital expenditure is ramping up aggressively with Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) standing at Rs 1.77 Cr for March 2026, representing a massive 1866.7% surge over the prior year [E40]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 10 years is a sluggish 1% [E14], 5-year growth is flat at 0% [E15], and 3-year growth has contracted by -8% [E16].

Sunil Healthcare Ltd is being under-appreciated because its fundamental earnings power has drastically outpaced its stock price movement over the medium term, with profit growing 65% compared to a price increase of only 14% over a 5-year period [E52]. This divergence is further highlighted by recent performance where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 1253%, indicating that the company is beginning to outperform market expectations [E53]. From an asset and valuation standpoint, the company trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.10x on a book value of 66.1 against a share price of 72.4 [E2], and its provider-measured P/B of 1.37x remains significantly discounted compared to the sector benchmark of 2.73x [E7]. Furthermore, the business is actively investing in its future capacity, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) surging by 1866.7% to reach Rs 1.77 Cr by March 2026, marking a clear growth spend underway [E40]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has remained stagnant or negative over multi-year periods, including -8% over 3 years and 0% over 5 years [E15, E16].
